groups.statement: The outer container nodes of the general PACS section, from the root down to the literature branch.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from outermost container to the literature branch.

groups.statement: Announcements and organizational activities are the kinds of community events and news in physics.
groups.rank_note: Parent heading first, then its child activity types.

groups.statement: Book-length and collected publications are kinds of physics literature issued as volumes or proceedings.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS order of the volume-type entries.

groups.statement: Teaching-oriented publications are kinds of literature written for instruction in physics.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS order of the teaching-related entries.

groups.statement: Review and commentary pieces are kinds of literature that survey, list, or comment on other work.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS order of the review-type entries.

groups.statement: Textbooks and schools are educational materials and institutions defined by the level of student they serve.
groups.rank_note: ordered from graduate to elementary level

groups.statement: General education and research topics concern the design, study and theory of physics education as a field.
groups.rank_note: ordered from general field to specific research areas

groups.statement: Teaching practice and training topics concern how teachers are prepared and how instruction and testing are carried out.
groups.rank_note: ordered from general training to specific methods

groups.statement: Educational aids and school-level categories cover the settings and tools used for science instruction in schools.
groups.rank_note: ordered from school settings to teaching aids

groups.statement: Computer use in education covers the ways computers and software are used in teaching and laboratories.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification listing.

groups.statement: Laboratory and demonstration work covers the apparatus, experiments and courses used for hands-on physics teaching.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification listing.

groups.statement: Audiovisual and artistic media are the sound, video and visual materials used to communicate physics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification listing.

groups.statement: Assessment, contests and classroom content covers testing, competitions, toy physics and errors in teaching materials.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification listing.

groups.statement: Logic and algebra topics are the foundational branches of set-theoretic and algebraic mathematics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification listing.

groups.statement: Rings, knots and general methods are mathematical topics applied within physics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification listing.

groups.statement: Linear and matrix algebra topics deal with vector spaces, tensors and matrices as constant-free mathematical tools.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from linear algebra to multilinear algebra to matrix theory.

groups.statement: Group-theoretic topics cover abstract groups, classical and Lie groups, their algebras, and quantum groups as symmetry structures.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general group theory to specific types of groups.

groups.statement: Further group-theoretic topics concern Lie algebras and infinite-dimensional or quantum deformations of groups.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from Lie algebras to infinite-dimensional groups to quantum groups.

groups.statement: Function theory and analysis topics cover measure, potential theory, complex analysis, special functions and differential equations.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general function theory to specific equation types.

groups.statement: Differential-equation and discrete-structure topics cover ordinary and partial equations, integrable systems, and combinatorics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from ordinary equations to partial equations to discrete graph theory.

groups.statement: Equation, series and expansion methods are scale-free analysis tools that no physical constant sets.
groups.rank_note: Least connected to c, ħ, G and N: purely formal analysis with no constant setting the scale.

groups.statement: Harmonic, integral and operator methods are abstract analysis whose link to ħ arises only through quantum applications.
groups.rank_note: Slightly more connected: operator and transform methods are the mathematical language of ħ-scale quantum theory.

groups.statement: Operational, variational, control and inverse methods together with geometry-and-topology as a field are general frameworks that connect to physical constants only through the problem they are applied to.
groups.rank_note: Intermediate: variational and control frameworks apply across c, ħ, G scales depending on the problem.

groups.statement: Specific geometries are the structures nearest to relativity and gravitation, where c and G set the scale of curvature.
groups.rank_note: Most connected to c and G: Riemannian and differential geometry underlie general relativity.

groups.statement: Topology and geometry of spaces study the shape and connectivity of manifolds and related spaces without any physical constant.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general topology to manifold structures.

groups.statement: Global analysis, singularity theory and geometric mechanics apply analytic methods to manifolds and mechanical structures in a constant-free way.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from analysis to singularities to mechanics.

groups.statement: Probability theory and stochastic processes describe random phenomena abstractly, independent of physical scales.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general probability to specific process types.

groups.statement: Statistical and decision-theoretic methods treat distributions, multivariate data and inference as formal tools with no intrinsic physical scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from decision theory to distributions to inference.

groups.statement: Numerical approximation methods compute solutions algorithmically, with scale set by the problem rather than by c, ħ, G or N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general numerical analysis to specific techniques.

groups.statement: Numerical analysis algorithms approximate, differentiate, integrate and optimize functions without any physical constant setting their scale.
Discretization methods turn differential and integral equations into finite problems, with the scale set by the problem and not by c, ħ, G or N.
Particle, statistical and Monte Carlo simulation methods depend on the particle number N and, for quantum Monte Carlo, on ħ.
Monte Carlo justifications and applications together with quantum, relativistic and classical field theories have scales set by ħ, c and N.
Classical field theories have no quantum scale, so their scale is set by c, and by G for gravity-like fields.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the standard Maxwell theory to other special classical field theories.

groups.statement: General quantum-mechanical frameworks and formalisms are scaled by ħ alone, independent of any particular system.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the broadest heading to the most specific mathematical method.

groups.statement: Wave-equation and scattering problems in quantum mechanics are scaled by ħ together with system parameters, and by c when relativistic.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from bound states to scattering to relativistic wave equations.

groups.statement: Single-system quantum mechanics topics whose scale is set by ħ, covering the semiclassical limit, foundations, phases, state reconstruction and tunneling.
groups.rank_note: structure

groups.statement: Multi-system topics where ħ and the number of systems N together set the scale, covering entanglement, decoherence and quantum information.
groups.rank_note: structure

groups.statement: Quantum information topics cover the communication, computation, entanglement and error-protection tasks that use quantum states.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Matter-wave optics topics treat atoms and neutrons as waves that can be steered and made to interfere.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Condensate property topics describe the static, dynamic, topological, spinor and entanglement behaviour of Bose-Einstein condensates.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Other degenerate quantum gas topics include miscellaneous condensation phenomena, atom lasers and degenerate Fermi gases.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Metrology topics concern measurement, its error theory, and the units and standards on which measurements rest.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Constants, units and standards define the foundation that fixes the scale of any physical measurement.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from constants to units to standards.

groups.statement: Mechanical measured quantities such as length, mass, time and velocity are scaled by c, ħ, G and N through their units.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from space to mass to time to motion.

groups.statement: Basic electromagnetic quantities are measured quantities whose scale depends on c and on other fundamental constants.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure.

groups.statement: Laboratory procedures are practical techniques for preparing, handling, testing and safely carrying out experiments.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from preparation to testing to safety.

groups.statement: Computing hardware and fluid turbulence are further topics treated with instruments and computation in experimental physics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure.

groups.statement: Computational methods that process, analyse, model and visualize data once it has been gathered.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 07.05 listing.

groups.statement: Methods and hardware for planning measurements, acquiring signals, interfacing with computers, and controlling systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 07.05 and 07.07 listing.

groups.statement: Equipment that senses physical quantities, converts them to signals, or displays and records them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 07.07 listing.

groups.statement: Mechanical instruments and devices that measure or manage force, strain, mass and vibration, including micromechanical systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 07.10 listing.

groups.statement: Thermal measuring and heating apparatus covers instruments that sense, hold or generate temperature and heat.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS section.

groups.statement: Low-temperature and heat-transfer machinery covers equipment that cools or moves heat to do work.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS section.

groups.statement: Vacuum production and measurement apparatus covers the general category plus gas removal, pumping and pressure gauging.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS section.

groups.statement: Vacuum containment and verification equipment covers the testing of seals and the chambers that hold a vacuum.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS section.

groups.statement: Electrical instrument components cover the general category plus circuits, noise control and charge measurement.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS section.

groups.statement: Signal handling and field generation equipment covers electronics that process signals and magnets that produce fields.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS section.

groups.statement: Magnetic instruments measure magnetic fields, moments and magnetization, or shield against magnetic fields.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing: field, moment, shielding.

groups.statement: Infrared and radio-frequency instruments generate, detect or analyze radiation from the infrared through the microwave and radiowave bands.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing: general, sources, detectors, spectrometers.

groups.statement: Optical measurement instruments quantify light intensity, polarization, refractive properties or interference.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Optical imaging and spectral instruments magnify, resolve or guide visible and ultraviolet light.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Particle sources, detectors and scanning probes work with atoms, molecules, charged particles or a scanned physical tip.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Scanning probe microscopes image surfaces by sensing a local tunneling, optical, or force interaction with a sharp tip.
X-ray and gamma-ray hardware generates, steers, and detects high-energy photons, whose scale is set by ħ and c.
X-ray analysis instruments use diffraction, spectroscopy, or imaging to probe the structure of matter.
Continuum flow regimes are characterized by how fluid motion behaves in smooth, bounded, wavy, or nonlinear conditions.
Numerical methods for fluid problems discretize boundaries or average turbulent equations to compute flows.
Field-driven manipulation topics and the people who study them fall outside the instrument and flow-regime groups.
Fluid phenomena and properties are physical behaviours and kinds of fluid that classical fluid dynamics studies.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from material properties to flow phenomena.

groups.statement: Computational and mathematical methods are the equations and numerical techniques used to model fluid flow.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from governing equation to numerical techniques.

groups.statement: Education and classification concepts frame how physics is taught, reasoned about and catalogued.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from teaching to reasoning to the broad classification.

groups.statement: Classical field topics treat static or propagating fields and waves, including acoustics, electrostatics, magnetostatics and wave propagation.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general acoustics to specific classical field problems.

groups.statement: Radiation topics cover emission of electromagnetic radiation by moving charges, from the general heading to synchrotron, Cherenkov and free-electron-laser sources.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general electromagnetism heading to specific radiation types.

groups.statement: Beam species are distinguished by the charge and speed of the particles, with the relativistic limit set by c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general beam class to specific species.

groups.statement: Advanced acceleration and radiation phenomena are ways a charged particle gains energy or emits light, with scales set by c and ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from radiation to acceleration schemes.

groups.statement: Beam handling steps are the successive operations that inject, shape, transport and clean up a beam.
groups.rank_note: Ordered along the beamline from injection to collimation.

groups.statement: Beam elements and diagnostics are the devices and measures that focus a beam, limit its aberrations, and measure its profile and intensity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from focusing devices to measurement tools.

groups.statement: General optics topics are the broad fields of beam optics and light propagation that frame the more specific beam topics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from broad optics to geometrical optics.

groups.statement: Geometric optics topics treat light as rays and wave fronts, ignoring wave effects such as diffraction.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from basic ray tracing to design and aberration analysis.

groups.statement: Wave optics topics treat light as a wave whose propagation, transmission and absorption are described directly.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general wave description to specific propagation effects.

groups.statement: Classical wave phenomena of light, each governed by the speed of light c and the wavelength rather than by ħ, G or N.
groups.rank_note: Kinds are listed in structural order without ranking by degree.

groups.statement: Wave-optics phenomena and methods describe how light's wave nature, set by c and ħ, shapes the optical field.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure of the PACS 42.25 and 42.30 headings

groups.statement: Imaging and processing topics concern forming, transferring, and interpreting images by optical or computational means.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure of the PACS 42.30 headings

groups.statement: Classical wave-optical imaging and hologram types whose scale is set only by c through the wavelength, with no ħ, G or N entering.
Hologram recording, readout, measurement and application topics that remain classical, so only c fixes the scale of the claim.
Quantum optics topics about the statistics, states and fluctuations of light, whose scale is set by ħ through the photon quantum.
Quantum optics topics of light-matter interaction and cooperative behavior, whose scale is set by ħ together with the number N of atoms or photons involved.
Quantum optical effects are phenomena where the quantum of action ħ sets the scale of light's interference, momentum and measurement.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the most purely quantum (ħ-set) effect to the more mechanical one.

groups.statement: Gain-medium lasers are classified by the material in which stimulated emission occurs, such as gas, dye, chemical, semiconductor or solid.
Structured-cavity lasers are defined by the resonator or scattering geometry that confines light, from microcavities to random media.
Special-mechanism lasers rely on a particular pumping or scattering process, such as Raman gain, diode pumping or short-wavelength emission.
General laser theory and design topics cover the overall principles and engineering of laser systems rather than a specific type.
Laser operation topics cover how the cavity, gain and output of a laser are built and controlled in time.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.60 listing.

groups.statement: Laser dynamics and regime topics cover steady, unstable and relaxing operating behavior of lasers.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.60 listing.

groups.statement: Laser application topics are the fields in which laser light is put to practical or measurement use.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.62 listing.

groups.statement: Nonlinear scattering and susceptibility topics describe how intense light drives material responses and scattering.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.65 listing.

groups.statement: Nonlinear propagation and conversion topics describe how intense beams change shape, phase and frequency in a medium.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.65 listing.

groups.statement: Parametric processes are nonlinear optical effects in which light is converted or amplified through second-order wave mixing.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.65 listing.

groups.statement: Nonlinear dynamics and pulse phenomena cover time-dependent, switching, soliton and guided-wave behavior of intense light.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.65 listing.

groups.statement: Eye-related topics treat the anatomy, optics and physiology of the visual organ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the PACS 42.66 listing.

groups.statement: Vision topics concern how the eye and brain detect, adapt to, scale, and interpret light and color.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from detection and adaptation to scales and perception.

groups.statement: Atmospheric propagation topics concern how light travels through the air and is attenuated or disturbed along the path.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general propagation to specific path effects.

groups.statement: Atmospheric constituent topics concern how gases, clouds, and aerosols absorb and scatter light.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from gases to clouds to aerosols.

groups.statement: Atmospheric and ocean optics covers how light propagates, scatters and forms images through natural media.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code within 42.68.

groups.statement: Glass, crystal and organic optical materials are passive solids and liquids chosen for their transmission and structural properties.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code within 42.70.

groups.statement: Active and responsive optical materials change or generate light through gain, recording, nonlinearity or band structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code within 42.70.

groups.statement: Photonic bandgap materials control light propagation through periodic structure rather than bulk composition.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code within 42.70.

groups.statement: Optical sources are devices that emit infrared, visible and ultraviolet light.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code within 42.72.

groups.statement: Passive optical elements shape, filter, split or steer light by geometry and material properties alone.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the passive element.

groups.statement: Active or functional optical devices collect, guide, process, modulate or display light for a system purpose.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the device system.

groups.statement: Imaging and sensing devices capture or measure light fields, with speed c setting timing and range scales.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by function as devices that image or sense light.

groups.statement: Devices that convert, carry, process, store or coat with light, where photon energy ħω and c set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the most direct dependence on photon energy (frequency conversion) to the least (coatings).

groups.statement: Fiber fundamentals cover how optical fibers are made, measured, and how light propagates and is polarized in them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general heading through fabrication, measurement, propagation and polarization.

groups.statement: Fiber devices and systems are the functional components and networks built from optical fibers.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from individual devices to couplers and networks.

groups.statement: Integrated optics covers the design, fabrication, interconnection and waveguiding of optical circuits on a chip.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general heading through design, fabrication, interconnects and waveguides.

groups.statement: Hybrid and other integrated systems together with optical testing and property characterization form the supporting and miscellaneous topics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from integrated hybrids to testing and general properties.

groups.statement: Broad physics fields outside classical mechanics proper, covering fluid-scale devices, sound and thermal transport.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS outline.

groups.statement: Classical mechanics of discrete systems and its formalisms, whose scale is set by Newtonian quantities rather than c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS outline.

groups.statement: Computational methods used in classical mechanics, including variational, perturbative and geometrical techniques.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS outline.

groups.statement: General dynamical principles of classical mechanics relate forces, momentum and energy without any scale-setting constant.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from formalism to forces and conserved quantities.

groups.statement: Rigid-body topics describe how extended solid bodies rotate and translate under classical mechanics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from rotational dynamics to kinematics and gyroscopic motion.

groups.statement: Single-body and general motion topics are set by classical dynamics alone, with N equal to one or a few bodies and no scale from c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Weakest dependence on N: one or a few bodies, no fundamental-constant scale.

groups.statement: Particle-system topics treat several interacting bodies, so N enters as a modest number, and only celestial mechanics brings in G.
groups.rank_note: Moderate dependence on N: few to many interacting bodies, with G relevant only for celestial mechanics.

groups.statement: Granular-system topics concern very many grains, so the scale of the claim is set by N with no role for c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Strong dependence on N: very large numbers of grains determine collective behaviour.

groups.statement: Continuum-mechanics topics take the limit of N going to infinity, so the scale is set by material parameters instead of by c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Strongest dependence on N: the continuum limit where individual bodies are no longer resolved.

groups.statement: Theoretical studies of static elasticity and granular traffic models are idealised descriptions whose scale comes from N or material constants only.
groups.rank_note: Strong to continuum dependence on N, as idealised models of many-body systems.

groups.statement: Elasticity and vibration topics describe how deformable solids respond to thermal, electromagnetic and dynamic loading and carry waves.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering within section 46.

groups.statement: Structural applications of continuum mechanics treat specific engineered forms such as beams, plates, shells, membranes, rods and strings.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering within 46.70.

groups.statement: General fluid dynamics theory covers the field itself and its mathematical, Hamiltonian and dynamical-systems formulations.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering from the section heading downward.

groups.statement: The governing equations of fluid motion are the conservation laws, constitutive relations and the Navier-Stokes equations.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Computational methods in fluid dynamics are numerical discretization schemes for solving the flow equations.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Numerical methods for simulating fluid flow, each discretizing the problem in a different way.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Broad categories of laminar flow defined by the dominant physical regime or idealization of the fluid.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Laminar flows defined by the geometry or confinement in which they occur, such as layers, wakes, jets, channels and films.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Laminar flow topics concerning thin-gap flow and the onset of instability in flows.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Instabilities that arise from material or interfacial properties of the fluid such as surface tension, viscosity, density contrast and phase change.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from bulk inviscid and viscous instabilities to interface-driven ones.

groups.statement: Instabilities that arise from the geometry and structure of the flow itself, such as shear, boundary layers, rotation and nonlinear bifurcation.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from primary flow instabilities to nonlinear and secondary developments.

groups.statement: Topics on the onset and basic nature of turbulence, including receptivity to disturbances, transition and coherent structures.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from onset of disturbances to established turbulent structure.

groups.statement: Topics on developed turbulence regimes and on the means of simulating, modeling and controlling them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from idealized regimes to wall-bounded flow, then modeling and control.

groups.statement: Theoretical and closure-based approaches describe turbulence analytically through statistical, dynamical, field-theoretic and Reynolds-stress models.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general statistical theory to specific closure models.

groups.statement: Flow phenomena and numerical simulation methods cover the physical settings of turbulence and the direct or large-eddy computations used to resolve them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from physical phenomena to simulation methods.

groups.statement: Turbulence bounded by walls or confining surfaces is a kind of wall-bounded flow, such as boundary layers, channels and pipes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Turbulence in free shear flows and transport processes covers wakes, jets, mixing layers, diffusion and convective heat transfer.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Vortex dynamics entries cover the motion of vortices and rotating fluids in classical fluid flow.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Vortex structure and dynamics covers how vortices interact, become unstable, reconnect as rings, and form regular streets.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Rotating and separated flows are flow states shaped by rotation or by detachment of the flow from a boundary.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Restoring-force wave types are waves named for the force or medium property that restores the disturbed fluid, such as gravity, surface tension, shear, compression or magnetic tension.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS numbering.

groups.statement: General and nonlinear wave phenomena cover hydrodynamic waves broadly, together with solitary waves, breaking waves and the interaction of waves with structures.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Compressible flow regimes are classified by flow speed relative to the speed of sound, from subsonic through transonic to supersonic, including shocks.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Rarefied gas dynamics covers gas flows where molecular mean free path matters and the continuum description fails.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS hierarchy, from the general heading to its subtopics.

groups.statement: Non-Newtonian fluid flow topics concern fluids whose stress does not vary linearly with strain rate, and how they are modeled, measured and destabilized.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS hierarchy, from the general heading to its subtopics.

groups.statement: Nonlinear collective phenomena are cases where a front or ordered structure emerges across a continuum medium.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS hierarchy, with the wave phenomenon before pattern formation.

groups.statement: Fluid-dynamics topics in the PACS 47.54 and 47.55 classification, listed as kinds of treatment of flow patterns and multiphase flows.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS 47.54 to 47.55 numbering.

groups.statement: Multiphase flows are fluid flows in which two or more phases or components move together, and each entry names a different arrangement of those phases.
groups.rank_note: Entries follow PACS listing order, not a ranking.

groups.statement: Bubble and drop phenomena concern the formation, motion, merging and phase-change behavior of discrete gas or liquid inclusions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from formation through dynamics and breakup to phase change.

groups.statement: Surface-driven flows and spreading are motions powered by interfacial tension gradients, surfactants, and wetting interactions with solid surfaces.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from surfactant and thermal drivers to resulting spreading and surface interactions.

groups.statement: Interface geometries and contact configurations are the shapes that fluid interfaces take, such as bridges, sheets and lines where phases meet.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general interfacial category to specific geometries.

groups.statement: Convective flows are fluid motions driven by buoyancy, temperature or concentration differences, or by surface tension variation.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general buoyancy-driven flow to specific convection types.

groups.statement: Particle-laden and complex multiphase systems are fluids whose behavior depends on dispersed solid, liquid or gas phases.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from fluidized solids to colloids and then foams and emulsions.

groups.statement: Particulate and dispersed media are fluids whose behavior is set by suspended grains or particles.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from coarse grains to fine colloids.

groups.statement: Molecularly structured complex fluids owe their flow behavior to the shape and organization of their molecules.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from ordered phases to long chains to mixed phases.

groups.statement: Transport and rheological phenomena describe how complex fluids deform, move and exchange material under forcing.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from bulk rheology to particle transport to charge effects.

groups.statement: Confined channel, nozzle and vessel flows are driven through bounded conduits, including biological ones.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general quasi-one-dimensional flows to specific conduits to biological flows.

groups.statement: Micro- and nano-scale flows are fluid behavior at small length scales where surface and non-continuum effects matter.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general field to specific small-scale phenomena.

groups.statement: Biological flows are set by classical continuum scales, where viscosity and size alone fix the Reynolds number and no fundamental constant enters.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from low-Reynolds-number viscous regime to high-Reynolds-number inertial regime.

groups.statement: Low-Reynolds-number motion and transport in biological media are governed by viscous continuum scales and the many-molecule number N that sets diffusion and delivery.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from flow regime to transport of many molecules.

groups.statement: Electromagnetically coupled fluids and plasma flows have scales that depend on the speed of light c through field coupling.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from field-responsive liquids to plasma dynamos where c-related coupling is strongest.

groups.statement: Reactive, radiative and nonequilibrium flows have scales set by molecular number N and by radiation involving c and ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from general reactive flows to radiation gas dynamics.

groups.statement: Measurement methods in fluid dynamics are classical probes whose scales are set by the flow and instrument, not by fundamental constants.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from general instrumentation to specific measured quantities.

groups.statement: Core applied fluid fields are the broad branches that treat engineered fluid systems, from the general field to specific areas.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general field to specific areas.

groups.statement: Flow control techniques are the kinds of methods used to modify and steer fluid flow behavior.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general category to specific techniques.

groups.statement: Material processing flows are the kinds of industrial flows in which fluids shape, coat or lubricate materials.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general category to specific processes.

groups.statement: Fluid-related physical systems are the kinds of specialized fluid media and accelerator hardware outside conventional flow engineering.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, with the hardware item first and the fluid medium second.

groups.statement: Classical physics subfields are the kinds of branches of physics that rest on classical, non-quantum laws.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general field to its subfields.

groups.statement: Accelerator and synchrotron topics are relativistic machines whose scale is set largely by the speed of light c.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by accelerator subtopic, no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Fluid flow regimes and simulation methods describe continuum fluid behavior governed by dimensionless numbers rather than by fundamental constants.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by flow regime and method, no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Fluid topics tied to specific settings, such as devices, media, and astrophysical systems, are scaled by N and G in addition to continuum properties.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by physical setting, no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Education, community, and instrumentation categories are not governed by any physical constant and are classified as general topics.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by general topic, no ranking implied.

groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general theory of currents to current algebras, sum rules and Regge methods.

groups.statement: S-matrix topics are kinds of analytic constraint on scattering amplitudes, such as analyticity, exact solutions and dispersion relations.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general S-matrix theory to analytic properties, exact S matrices and dispersion relations.

groups.statement: Relativistic scattering formalism and kinematics set their scale by c and ħ alone, since they describe general S-matrix structure without any specific coupling.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general scattering framework to its kinematic and angular-momentum decomposition.

groups.statement: Approximation and many-body scattering methods set their scale by c and ħ together with the particle number N, because they handle several channels or several scatterers.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from approximation schemes to multi-channel and many-body treatments.

groups.statement: Unified field theories and models set their scale by c, ħ and G, since they try to combine the interactions, possibly with gravity, and relate their couplings.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general class of unified theories to strong-electroweak unification and coupling relations.

groups.statement: Electroweak flavor and mixing claims set their scale by c and ħ through quark and lepton masses and CKM mixing parameters.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general electroweak theory to flavor parameters and their determination.

groups.statement: Electroweak process predictions and quantum electrodynamics calculations set their scale by c and ħ through the fine-structure coupling in specific processes and tests.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from electroweak applications and corrections to QED calculations and tests.

groups.statement: The general framework of QCD sets the fundamental scale of the strong interaction through the coupling, confinement, and experimental checks of the theory.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the overarching theory to its general properties and experimental tests.

groups.statement: Calculational methods extract QCD predictions either perturbatively in the small coupling or nonperturbatively on the lattice and by other means.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from perturbative expansions to resummation to nonperturbative techniques.

groups.statement: Collective and exotic states of strongly interacting matter are described by thermal ensembles, deconfined plasma, and multi-quark or gluonic bound states.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from deconfined plasma to exotic hadron states to statistical and other models.

groups.statement: Phenomenological quark models describe hadrons as bound states of constituent quarks, with differing treatments of confinement and relativistic effects.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general class of quark models to specific bag, nonrelativistic, relativistic, and potential variants.

groups.statement: Effective-theory approaches reduce QCD to simpler low-energy or heavy-quark descriptions by exploiting symmetries and separating scales.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from chiral and soliton descriptions to heavy-quark theory and factorization.

groups.statement: Phenomenological hadron models describe strong-interaction behavior and hadron properties using effective frameworks scaled by ħ, c and the strong coupling.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from scattering models to mass models.

groups.statement: Models beyond the standard model extend the known gauge, Higgs or matter content, setting their scale by new physics above the electroweak constants.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from the general category to specific extensions.

groups.statement: Composite models and atomic and molecular collisions treat systems built from constituents, with the scale set by binding of those parts.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from the substructure model to the collision category.

groups.statement: Leptonic, semileptonic and radiative meson decays are weak or electromagnetic transitions of specific meson families, with scales set by c, ħ and the weak or fine-structure couplings.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from the general category to specific meson families.

groups.statement: Quarkonium, bottom-meson, other-meson and hadronic pion decays are meson decays whose rates are governed by the strong interaction and heavy-quark masses.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from quarkonia to hadronic decays.

groups.statement: Light mesons and baryons are hadrons whose weak and strong decay modes are classified together by decaying hadron.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from meson decays to baryon decays and their sub-modes.

groups.statement: Heavy-flavor mesons are mesons containing charm or bottom quarks, including quarkonia, whose decays are classified together.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, by increasing heavy quark mass.

groups.statement: Lepton decays are the decays of the charged leptons and heavy neutrinos through the weak interaction.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general category to specific leptons.

groups.statement: Intermediate boson decays are the decays of the W and Z bosons that carry the weak force.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general category to W and Z.

groups.statement: Electromagnetic processes and properties cover masses, moments, form factors and decays governed by the electromagnetic interaction.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general category to specific properties.

groups.statement: Photon and charged-lepton interactions with hadrons, including electromagnetic corrections, are set in scale by c and ħ through the electromagnetic coupling.
groups.rank_note: ordered from the general category to specific scattering and production types

groups.statement: Baryon production and lepton-lepton collisions producing hadrons and leptons are scaled by c and ħ through the center-of-mass energy of the colliding leptons.
groups.rank_note: ordered from the general lepton-lepton category to specific e-e+ final states

groups.statement: High-energy electroweak, Higgs, new-physics and super-high-energy hadronic processes are scaled by c and ħ at the highest available energies.
groups.rank_note: ordered from e-e+ precision and heavy-boson processes to the highest-energy hadron reactions

groups.statement: Low- and intermediate-energy nucleon and hyperon reactions are scaled by c and ħ through the strong-interaction range and the nucleon mass.
groups.rank_note: ordered from the general category to nucleon, hyperon and pion interactions

groups.statement: Kaon-baryon and meson-meson interactions are scaled by c and ħ through the meson masses and strong-interaction range.
groups.rank_note: ordered from meson-baryon to meson-meson scattering

groups.statement: Hadron collision processes are classified by the scattering outcome, with cross sections whose scale is set by ħ and c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from elastic to inelastic to total cross section.

groups.statement: Inclusive production measurements are classified by which particles are detected or bounded in a collision, including cosmic-ray interactions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from identified hadrons to nonhadronic particles to limits to cosmic rays.

groups.statement: Jets in large-Q2 scattering are described by the stages of their formation, from the general phenomenon through production to fragmentation into hadrons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general jets to production to fragmentation.

groups.statement: Baryons are classified by their flavor content and type, from nucleons to resonances, hyperons and charmed baryons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general class to nucleons, resonances, hyperons and charmed baryons.

groups.statement: Other specific particle categories include the general properties heading, bottom and exotic baryons, and mesons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general heading to bottom baryons, exotic baryons and mesons.

groups.statement: Mesons are quark-antiquark hadrons that differ by the flavour content of their constituent quarks.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from light flavour-free mesons through strange, charmed and bottom to exotic states.

groups.statement: Charged leptons are the electrically charged point-like fermions that do not feel the strong force, distinguished by generation and mass.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the electron through the muon and tau to heavier hypothetical leptons.

groups.statement: Neutrino topics cover the neutral, weakly interacting leptons, including their ordinary, massive and non-standard forms.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from ordinary neutrinos to mass and mixing to non-standard neutrinos.

groups.statement: Quark flavours are the distinct types of quark, each characterized by its own flavour and mass.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from light quarks through charm, bottom and top to further quarks.

groups.statement: Overview headings and heavy bound states link the general lepton and quark categories to quark-antiquark systems of heavy flavours.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general lepton and quark headings to the heavy quarkonium bound states.

groups.statement: Massless gauge bosons of the unbroken forces have scales set by c and ħ alone, with the number of colours N entering for gluons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the setting constants

groups.statement: Massive electroweak gauge bosons have scales set by ħ and c together with the Higgs-given mass.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the setting constants

groups.statement: Higgs and scalar-sector particles have scales set by the vacuum expectation value and the breaking of symmetry.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the setting constants

groups.statement: Hypothetical new-physics particles have scales set by N-dependent new couplings or by extra structure beyond the standard model.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the setting constants

groups.statement: Technicolor and leptoquarks are hypothesized particles beyond the Standard Model whose claims are scaled by the fundamental constants c, ħ, G and N.
Broad nuclear-domain headings whose claims are scaled by the nucleon number N and the nuclear interaction scale, with ħ and c entering only as background constants.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the broadest heading (nuclear physics as a whole) to the narrower ones (structure, then properties of nuclei).

groups.statement: Bulk static properties of a nucleus whose magnitudes are set by the nucleon number N together with ħ and c through the nucleon size and mass scales.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the most N-dependent bulk quantity (binding energy and mass) to the distribution-based quantities.

groups.statement: Quantum-number and moment properties of nuclear states whose scale is fixed by ħ, with c entering through the electromagnetic moments and N through the number of nucleons.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the purely ħ-quantized property (spin and parity) to the properties that also need c and N.

groups.statement: Theoretical models and level descriptions of the nucleus whose scale depends on N collectively, with ħ setting the quantum level spacing.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the single-particle description (smallest N dependence) to the collective and few-body treatments.

groups.statement: Atomic and resonance phenomena whose scale is set by ħ and the interaction strength of the colliding or driven particles, independent of c, G and nuclear N.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the scattering resonance to the driven coherent optical process.

groups.statement: Nuclear force topics describe the interaction between nucleons and hadrons, with scale set by ħ and c through meson exchange and effective interactions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from vacuum forces to effective hadronic interactions.

groups.statement: Few-body topics treat systems of two or three nucleons, where the number N of bodies is small and fixes the scale of the problem.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from the general few-body class to two-nucleon and three-nucleon systems.

groups.statement: Microscopic and algebraic model methods build nuclear structure from many-body quantum mechanics, where ħ and the nucleon number N set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from the general heading to the ab initio, mean-field and stochastic computational methods.

groups.statement: Collective and symmetry-based nuclear models describe structure through shells, clusters, collective modes and group-theoretical symmetries rather than full microscopic calculation.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from the shell model to collective, group-theoretical and cluster descriptions.

groups.statement: Bulk matter and decay topics concern large-N nuclear and quark matter and radioactive decay, where thermodynamic limits and the weak interaction set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from nuclear matter in general to its asymmetric, symmetry-energy, meson, equation-of-state and quark forms, then decay.

groups.statement: Electromagnetic transition measurements are scaled by the fine-structure coupling built from c and ħ, which fixes photon emission rates and angular patterns.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from measurement methods to the quantities they extract.

groups.statement: Gamma-ray energy and electron-emission processes are scaled by c and ħ through photon energies and the conversion of nuclear excitation into atomic electrons or pairs.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from gamma emission to the processes that replace it.

groups.statement: Beta decay and capture processes are scaled by the weak coupling together with c and ħ, which set lepton emission rates tied to nuclear structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general weak processes to nuclear-structure links.

groups.statement: Quantum many-body and wave-based reaction models are scaled by ħ and c, treating nuclear scattering through wave equations and relativistic dynamics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general reaction models to specific wave-based formulations.

groups.statement: Statistical and bulk-flow reaction models are scaled by the particle number N, which governs ensemble behaviour through sampling, hydrodynamics and thermal averages.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from numerical sampling to continuum and thermal descriptions.

groups.statement: Resonance reactions are nuclear reactions dominated by collective or discrete resonant excitations of the nucleus.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 24.30 subtree: general heading, then giant resonances, then other resonances.

groups.statement: Statistical reaction theories describe nuclear reactions through averaged behaviour, fluctuations and chaos among many overlapping levels.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 24.60 subtree: general heading, then compound-nucleus, multistep direct, fluctuation and chaos entries.

groups.statement: Photonuclear reactions are nuclear reactions in which a real photon is absorbed, scattered or used to produce particles.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 25.20 subtree: general heading, then absorption and scattering, then photoproduction.

groups.statement: Electron scattering reactions probe nuclear structure by scattering electrons elastically or inelastically from the nucleus.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 25.30 subtree: general heading, then elastic, then inelastic to specific states, then inelastic to continuum.

groups.statement: Other lepton-induced reactions use positrons, muons, neutrinos or electroproduction to probe nuclei through leptonic interactions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 25.30 subtree: positron, muon, neutrino, then electroproduction entries.

groups.statement: Scattering processes leave projectile and target intact, changing only their direction or excitation.
groups.rank_note: Ranked least to most disruptive: elastic scattering first, then inelastic scattering.

groups.statement: Transfer reactions move one or more nucleons between projectile and target nuclei.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by increasing projectile mass: nucleon-induced, then light-ion, then heavy-ion transfer.

groups.statement: Charge-exchange reactions change the charge state of the colliding nucleons while the mass number stays fixed.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by increasing projectile mass: nucleon-induced, then light-ion, then heavy-ion charge exchange.

groups.statement: High-energy and general-category entries cover meson production, spallation and broad classes of nucleon or unstable-nucleus induced reactions.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the broad general categories to the most violent reactions above meson production thresholds.

groups.statement: Inelastic neutron scattering and inelastic proton scattering are nuclear reactions in which an incident nucleon excites a target nucleus, so the claim's scale is set by the constants ħ and c together with the nucleon number N.
Fusion and capture processes have a scale set by ħ through quantum tunnelling of the Coulomb barrier and the joining of nuclei.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from light-ion fusion and capture to heavy-ion fusion and the compound nucleus.

groups.statement: Transfer and charge-exchange reactions have a scale set by ħ through the quantum overlap of nuclear wave functions when nucleons or charge pass between nuclei.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, with light-ion reactions before heavy-ion reactions and transfer before charge exchange.

groups.statement: Scattering, excitation and resonance processes have a scale set by ħ through the de Broglie wavelength and the diffraction of the colliding nuclei.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from total cross sections through elastic scattering and Coulomb excitation to resonances.

groups.statement: Fragmentation and breakup processes have a scale set by the number N of nucleons that the colliding nuclei split into.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from simple breakup to strongly damped collisions and multifragment emission.

groups.statement: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions have a scale set by the speed of light c because the collision energies approach relativistic values.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by how strongly relativistic each entry is, from the general low-energy heading to the hard-scattering regime.

groups.statement: Heavy-ion collision observables are the particles, photons and correlations measured to characterize relativistic nuclear collisions.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS numbering order.

groups.statement: Pion-induced reactions are nuclear processes in which an incident pion scatters elastically, inelastically, by charge exchange, or is absorbed.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS numbering order.

groups.statement: Strange-particle and general meson-induced reactions are nuclear processes initiated by kaons, hyperons or mesons in general.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS numbering order.

groups.statement: Fission reactions are nuclear splitting processes distinguished by whether they occur spontaneously or are induced by neutrons, charged particles or photons.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS numbering order.

groups.statement: Nuclear astrophysics covers nuclear processes in stars, including nucleosynthesis during hydrostatic stellar burning.
groups.rank_note: Listed in PACS numbering order.

groups.statement: Quiescent stellar burning stages convert lighter nuclei into heavier ones in sequence over a star's lifetime.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from hydrogen burning to helium burning to s-process, late evolution and quasistatic processes.

groups.statement: Explosive nucleosynthesis environments produce nuclei rapidly under extreme temperature, density and neutron or neutrino flux.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by environment and process type.

groups.statement: Nuclear matter aspects of neutron stars are the regions and equation of state whose scale is set by gravity and nuclear interactions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the star's interior core to its crust to the matter equation of state.

groups.statement: Entries on specific nuclei and a truncated conformal space computational method are treated as structure-and-method topics rather than astrophysical processes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered with nuclear properties first and the computational method second.

groups.statement: Neutron physics for nuclear engineering covers how neutrons interact with matter through scattering and absorption.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general field to scattering to absorption.

groups.statement: Neutron-physics topics concern how neutrons interact with matter, a scale set by ħ and nuclear cross sections and by the nucleon number N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from neutron slowing and cross sections to the radiation emitted and imaged.

groups.statement: Reactor design and modelling covers the theory and simulation of the reactor as a whole, with the core scale set by neutron transport and the nuclear constants behind it.
groups.rank_note: General overview of fission reactors followed by the theory and design of the reactor.

groups.statement: Operation, safety and fuel-cycle topics cover control, instrumentation and protection of the plant, and the handling of fuel and radioactive waste.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from control and monitoring to fuel handling and waste disposal.

groups.statement: Reactor types are the kinds of fission reactor classified by their purpose, such as research, breeding, power production or propulsion.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general class of reactor types to specific applications.

groups.statement: This group collects the further nuclear-technology topics of radioactive waste disposal and instrumentation, where the claim's scale is set by the governing constants c, ħ, G and N.
Fusion reactor design and operation topics concern the plasma physics and fuel handling that determine whether a reactor can reach ignition.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 28.52 listing.

groups.statement: Fusion reactor hardware and safety topics concern the physical materials, components and safeguards that make up a reactor plant.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 28.52 listing.

groups.statement: Cyclic accelerators are machines that bend charged particles repeatedly around a closed path to raise their energy.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 29.20 listing.

groups.statement: Straight-path accelerators raise particle energy along a single line using static or oscillating electric fields.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 29.20 listing.

groups.statement: Particle sources supply the electrons, neutrons and polarized ions that experiments and accelerators use as beams or probes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 29.25 listing.

groups.statement: Sources and targets supply the ions, polarized nuclei and radioactive nuclei whose particle numbers N set the scale of the experiment.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from ion sources to targets to radioactive sources.

groups.statement: Accelerator beam physics covers the injection, transport, dynamics, characterization and polarization of beams whose speed approaches c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general beams heading through injection, dynamics, transport and characteristics to polarized beams.

groups.statement: Beam characteristics and electron and charged-particle spectrometers measure particle momentum and energy using fields, at scales set by c and ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from beam characteristics and polarized beams to spectrometers.

groups.statement: Spectroscopic techniques identify particles and photons by energy, with electron, charged-particle, neutron, and X- and γ-ray spectroscopy each probing quantum scales set by ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from electron through charged-particle and neutron to X- and γ-ray spectroscopy.

groups.statement: Radioactive-beam facilities and radiation detectors produce, reaccelerate and register exotic nuclei and radiation, with counting statistics governed by N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from radioactive beams in general through fast and reaccelerated beams to detectors.

groups.statement: Gas-filled and tracking detectors measure charged particles by the ionization they leave in a medium, with the signal scale set by the number N of ion pairs.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from simple counting to position-resolved devices.

groups.statement: Light-producing detectors convert particle energy into photons, with the scale set by the speed of light c in the medium or by quantum emission processes involving ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from threshold-velocity (c-dependent) to emission-based devices.

groups.statement: Data-handling methods process detector output, and their scale is set by the number N of recorded events rather than by physical constants.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general heading to specific acquisition and analysis tasks.

groups.statement: Atomic and molecular structure topics are governed by quantum mechanics, with the scale set by ħ and the number N of electrons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from broad headings to specific computational methods.

groups.statement: Electronic-structure calculation methods approximate many-electron quantum systems, where the scale is set by ħ and the electron number N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general techniques to specific correlation methods.

groups.statement: Relativistic treatments bring the speed of light c into the claim, so that its scale is set by c together with ħ through fine-structure corrections.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by how strongly c sets the scale, from fine-structure corrections to full relativistic many-body calculations.

groups.statement: Statistical, semi-empirical and tight-binding approaches approximate many electrons with simplified models whose scale is set by ħ and the particle number N.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the most empirical models to the more fundamental statistical ones, by how much N rather than detailed ħ dynamics sets the scale.

groups.statement: Density-functional formalisms express the many-electron problem through the electron density, with the scale set by ħ and the electron number N.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from formal foundations to specific functionals and time-dependent extensions, by increasing reliance on N-electron structure.

groups.statement: Correlated wavefunction methods solve the few- or many-electron Schrödinger problem, with the scale set by ħ and the number of electrons N.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from high-precision few-body calculations to approximate treatments of larger systems, by how strongly N sets the scale.

groups.statement: Property and application claims report measurable quantities whose scale is set mainly by ħ, with N controlling the size of the system.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from single-atom spectroscopic properties to molecular and condensed applications, by increasing dependence on N.

groups.statement: Correlation calculations for excited atomic states and for molecules treat the many-electron problem at a scale set by ħ and the electron number N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: atoms and ions, then diatomic, then polyatomic systems.

groups.statement: Numerical and variational schemes solve the Schrodinger equation computationally, at a scale set by ħ and the electron number N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from grid and coordinate methods to self-consistent and simulation methods.

groups.statement: Semiclassical, path-integral, group-theoretical and valence bond formalisms are built on ħ and on symmetry or classical-limit structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from classical-limit and path formalisms to symmetry and bonding formalisms.

groups.statement: Corrections to electronic structure from relativity, QED, hyperfine and isotope effects have scales set by c, through the fine-structure constant, together with ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general heading to relativistic and QED specifics.

groups.statement: Atomic-structure corrections whose scale is set by the speed of light c together with ħ, covering relativistic and quantum-electrodynamic effects such as negative-energy states, self-energy, and vacuum polarization on level energies.
Parity- and CP-violating weak-interaction effects in atoms have scales set by the weak coupling together with c and ħ.
Radiative and bound-state QED corrections in exotic and highly charged systems have scales set by c and ħ through the fine-structure constant.
Potential energy surfaces and their couplings describe nuclear motion with a scale set by ħ and the particle number N of the molecule.
Environmental effects, dynamics, and general atomic properties are scaled by ħ and the number N of interacting particles in the medium or sample.
Molecular solids and the properties of atoms are further subjects whose claims are set in scale by the governing constants c, ħ, G and N.
Static atomic properties describe how an atom's energy levels respond to fields and binding, with scales set by ħ, c and the fine-structure constant.
Spectral regions classify atomic spectra by the photon energy range, whose scale is set by ħ and c through the transition frequency.
Resonance and magnetic spectra concern transitions between closely spaced levels such as those driven by radio-frequency fields.
Photon-driven excitation and ionization processes are the ways an atom absorbs light to reach excited, ionized or detached states, with scales set by ħ and c.
Auger decay and coherent control are processes in which electron rearrangement or controlled light-atom coupling steers atomic transitions.
Nonlinear and resonant photon-atom processes have scales set by ħ and the light intensity, since energy is absorbed in quanta of ħω.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS 32.80 sequence.

groups.statement: The top-level headings frame molecular properties and spectra as a whole, covering the scope in which ħ and c govern molecular interactions with photons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the section heading to the property and spectra headings.

groups.statement: Geometric and energetic molecular properties have scales fixed by ħ through quantum binding and structure, without any explicit role for c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS 33.15 sequence.

groups.statement: Electromagnetic response and spectroscopic constants of molecules involve ħ together with c through couplings, moments and fine structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS 33.15 sequence.

groups.statement: Ensemble, dynamical and spectral measurements bring in N, the number of particles, with timing and photon scattering and absorption scales set by ħ and c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS 33.15 and 33.20 sequence.

groups.statement: Spectral-region topics classify molecular spectra by the wavelength band of radiation in which they are observed.
groups.rank_note: Listed in structure order, from visible to X-ray wavelengths.

groups.statement: Motion-analysis topics interpret molecular spectra in terms of rotation, vibration and their couplings with electronic motion.
groups.rank_note: Listed in structure order, from pure rotation and vibration to coupled motions.

groups.statement: Emission and decay topics cover how excited molecules give off light or lose energy without radiating.
groups.rank_note: Listed in structure order, from the general field to its specific subtopics.

groups.statement: Line-property topics describe the strengths, widths and shapes of molecular spectral lines and bands.
groups.rank_note: Listed in structure order, from the general field to specific properties.

groups.statement: Photon-driven process topics cover the ways light interacting with molecules changes their state, ionizes them or breaks them apart.
groups.rank_note: Listed in structure order, from field-driven effects to ionization and dissociation.

groups.statement: Photon-driven processes are those in which absorbing several photons excites or ionizes an atom or molecule, so that the field strength and ħ set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: ionization to highly excited states, then other multiphoton processes.

groups.statement: Interaction potentials and forces describe the energy between atoms or molecules as a function of their separation, which sets the scale of all collisions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: general collision field, general potentials, then interatomic and atom-molecule potentials.

groups.statement: Elastic and energy-transfer scattering covers heavy-particle collisions in which the projectile's energy is redistributed without necessarily changing the species involved.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: general atom and molecule scattering, stopping power, elastic and ultracold, then rotational and vibrational transfer.

groups.statement: Heavy-particle collisions that change the electronic state or chemical identity of the target include excitation, ionization, chemical reactions and laser-modified scattering.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: atomic excitation, molecular excitation, chemical reactions, laser-modified processes.

groups.statement: Electron and positron scattering covers collisions of light charged projectiles with atoms and molecules, from elastic scattering to dissociation and recombination.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: general electron and positron scattering, elastic, excitation and ionization, dissociation, then recombination and attachment.

groups.statement: Scattering processes and quantum computation are quantum phenomena whose scale is set by ħ and phase coherence.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from specific scattering types to quantum computation.

groups.statement: Exotic atoms replace ordinary constituents with unusual particles, so their scale is set by ħ and the particle masses.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general category to specific exotic atom types.

groups.statement: The chain-structure properties of macromolecules concern mass, sequence, conformation and bond geometry, where large N sets the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general macromolecules to detailed chain properties.

groups.statement: The spectral properties of macromolecules are the electronic and vibrational structure that depends on ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from electronic to vibrational and rotational spectra.

groups.statement: Atomic and molecular clusters are finite aggregates of N atoms whose electronic, magnetic and phase behavior depends on N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general cluster concept to specific properties.

groups.statement: Equilibrium properties of clusters are the structural, optical, collective and charge-related features set by electromagnetic constants and the number of atoms N.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by kind of static cluster property

groups.statement: Cluster change processes are the reactive, fragmenting and diffusive behaviors in which clusters evolve over time, scaled by ħ and N.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by kind of cluster dynamical process

groups.statement: Cooling methods are the techniques that reduce the kinetic energy of atoms, molecules and ions, with scales set by ħ and the speed of light c through photon momentum.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by kind of cooling technique and its umbrella headings

groups.statement: Trapping and light-force methods are the ways of confining or pushing atoms, molecules and ions with fields and light, scaled by ħ and c.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by kind of confinement or light-force technique

groups.statement: Fundamental-physics topics are the phenomenological, nuclear-astrophysical and hypothetical-particle subjects whose scales are set by c, ħ and G.
groups.rank_note: Grouped by kind of fundamental-physics subject

groups.statement: Atomic and molecular fields have their scale set chiefly by ħ together with the particle number N of the bound electrons and nuclei.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the broad atomic field to its specific atomic, molecular and residual sub-fields, with ħ and N dominant throughout.

groups.statement: Laser, photonic and spectroscopic fields have a scale set by ħ and c through light-matter interaction and photon propagation.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from lasers and nonlinear optics through photonics to the terahertz band, each set by ħ and c.

groups.statement: Cold-atom and degenerate-gas fields have a scale set by ħ and a very large particle number N acting as a coherent matter wave.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the general quantum-physics field to the specific gas and matter-wave systems, ħ and N dominant.
